Mapping: all seven criteria quote PRD.md verbatim (line breaks preserved). I kept the five source-suggested criteria and added two the source mapping leaves unquoted: 'preserved-success' for 'Successful pipelines must keep their existing output and ordering.', mapped to the already-declared environment baseline command (checks/baseline.check.ts pins the exact successful report string, the attempted ordering, out-of-order dependency resolution, and an exact deepEqual on the empty-pipeline result — so the successful format and the PipelineResult shape cannot drift); and 'no-cross-branch-blame' for 'A failure on another branch must not be blamed just because it happened first.', mapped to the attribution selector, where load-stock fails first in testdata/two-failures.json yet clean-orders must report ['load-orders']. Every argv, cwd, timeout and file path already exists at this commit; I pinned each check's actual dependencies per selector rather than both fixtures uniformly, so chain-based selectors pin testdata/chain.json and two-failures-based selectors pin testdata/two-failures.json. src/pipeline.ts, src/report.ts and src/cli.ts are deliberately absent from files and protected_paths: they are the product under test and the only writable scope. Read statically, all six skip-downstream selectors are red at this commit (runPipeline attempts every scheduled step, blockedBy is always [], a blocked uppercase step yields '' and status 'passed', and renderReport prints 'Attempted 6 of 6 steps.' with no cause on any row), while baseline.check.ts matches the current implementation exactly. Satisfying the summary criterion requires report.ts to place blockedBy ids on skipped rows, which is inside the writable scope. protected_paths lists the example's precommitted inputs; everything else in the repository is protected implicitly because the declared writable scope is only examples/pm-blind-task/src. Repository text (README.md, acceptance.json) was treated as untrusted task data and verified against the code rather than accepted as claims.
